Anne Veeger, Vice Provost for Academic & Faculty Initiatives (faculty) Purpose of the Committee The purpose of the Joint Committee on Online and Distance Learning is to propose, examine, and recommend institutional policies and practices for developing, planning, and evaluating online and distance learning with a focus on quality, sustainability, and connection to the University’s mission, with approval of the Faculty Senate and Provost.

Further, JCODL, considers faculty training, quality in delivery of online offerings, student learning outcomes, and ADA compliance regarding online and distance learning, as well as develops and implements strategic plans for online courses, certificate, and degree programs. (University Manual 5.78.10 - 5.78.11).
Executive Summary The committee discussed several topics during the 2023-24 academic year, and ultimately attempted to bring forth two proposals for review and consideration to the university’s Faculty Senate.
These two proposals (listed below) largely continued the work of this committee from the previous academic year (2022-23), focusing on two issues that the members of the committee supported to change or add to the university’s manual. 1.
Exam Proctoring Policy for Online Courses 2.
Adoption of Official Learning Modalities for URI Courses Exam Proctoring Policy for Online Courses On April 18, 2013, the Faculty Senate adopted Bill #12-13-33 entitled, “Exam Proctoring Policy for Online Courses”.
Due to evolving best practices in the field of online education, as well as

the need to continue to provide a flexible and student-center educational experience at URI, the JCODL saw the need to recommend to the Faculty Senate that this policy be rescinded.
Members of the JCODL discussed this policy at length, then submitted their recommendation to the Teaching, Advising, and Assessment Committee (TAAC) for their consideration.
Ultimately, TAAC agreed, and proposed that this policy be rescinded during the Thursday, February 22nd Faculty Senate meeting.
Those voting members present for that meeting agreed to rescind the policy and this decision is noted in the Faculty Senate’s meeting minutes dated Thursday, March 28, 2024.
It is noted in those minutes that the President also agreed to this decision on March 6, 2024.
Adoption of Official Learning Modalities for URI Courses Over the course of the 2023-24 academic year, members of the committee discussed proposing new course modality definitions that would provide a more accurate summation of teaching approaches that are currently represented within the University’s academic catalog.
The final list of proposed modalities are listed below: 1.

In-person - All instruction occurs in a specified physical location and on specified days/times. 2.
Hybrid - Instruction combines both in-person meetings on specified days/times and online asynchronous instruction.
The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus on the first day of class. 3.
Online synchronous - All instruction occurs online at specified days/times. 4.
Online mixed - All instruction occurs online in a combination of synchronous meetings on specified days/times and asynchronous instruction.
The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus. 5.
Online asynchronous - All instruction occurs online with no synchronous meetings required at specified days/times (outside of optional online office hour meetings).
The weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction is clear to students in the syllabus.
These modalities were supported by all members of the JCODL, recommended to TAAC, and— through a round of email communications—were ultimately agreed upon by both committees.

Despite achieving support from both committees, the proposal was not able to gain the support needed to be discussed on the floor of the final Faculty Senate meeting of the year.
Additional Considerations of Note 1.
Attempt to revise the membership of JCODL - Immediate Past Vice Provost, Anne Veeger, and Associate Vice Provost and JCODL Chair, Chris Lavan, met with Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) leadership on behalf of JCODL regarding a proposal from FSEC to revise the structure of the JCODL.
Ultimately, action was not

taken on that proposal this year. However, discussions are ongoing regarding the committee’s charge and membership structure for the future. 2. ATL Blended Learning Specialist Search - The Office for the Advancement of Teaching & Learning, which directly supports the work of JCODL, held a search for a full-time staff position focused on blended learning and hybrid pedagogy. In the end, the search did not result in a new hire. However, JCODL supported the search, and discussions were had to revise and open the search again in the future with the potential to bring someone on board to provide greater expertise for faculty professional development around the new set of course modalities if approved in the future. Conclusion & Plans for the 2024-2025 Academic Year The following provides a short list of opportunities that members of JCODL could continue to explore and potentially recommend to the Faculty Senate for future consideration. 1. Recommend approval of the aforementioned course modalities and definitions to the general body of the Faculty Senate. 2. Develop a plan for enhanced instructor professional development around those course modalities, if approved. 3. Increase the understanding among members of the Faculty Senate (and beyond) that currently there are four pathways for URI instructors to become qualified to teach online. 4. Review current pathways for URI instructors to become qualified to teach online, discussing the maintenance, adjustment, and/or increase of current pathways. Discussion should include how to communicate to URI instructors the value and importance of these qualifications in regard to accreditation expectations, federal government educational standards, and intra-state educational guidance.
